title: API Compact Suite PRD — scope negotiation, acceptance, and cutover plan
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose: ship a tightly scoped, production-ready compact suite that exposes four endpoint types (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) under a single minimal product bundle aimed at self-serve and early enterprise customers. This PRD formalizes the API contracts, non-functional SLO targets, acceptance criteria, negotiation levers (what we cut or defer), cutover plan, and observability/playbook for launch.

Goals: provide a lightweight entry bundle with predictable latency and unit cost, consistent behavioral guarantees across endpoints, and a straightforward migration path from legacy single-endpoint experiences. Target customers: PLG teams and developer platform teams who need predictable performance with a small surface area.

Non-goals: multi-model orchestration, advanced structured output tooling, private/VPC installs, and language-specific SDK feature parity for phase 1. Those are slated for follow-on releases (phase 2).

Success metrics (initial 8 weeks): 1) 99th percentile request latency below targets for each endpoint under the committed capacity lane; 2) no P0 incidents attributable to API contract mismatches; 3) integration churn < 10 support tickets in first month; 4) cost per 1k tokens within the expected budget for the compact bundle.

Audience: product, infra engineering, runtime, DX, QA, support, legal.
apis_and_contracts: /v1/compact/chat: streaming + non-streaming variants. Minimal request: {model, input, max_tokens, temperature}. Response: events chunked for streaming; final message object includes message.id, content, and usage tokens. Agent/tool-calling is explicitly out of scope for phase 1.

/v1/compact/completions: single-shot completion with prompt and optional prompt_type header. Backwards-compatible with existing completions surface except we remove legacy 'stop_sequence' in favor of 'stop' array (converter shim provided for 3 months).
/v1/compact/embeddings: single vector output per request. Contract: input up to 4096 tokens, deterministic encoding flag supported. Response: {model, embedding, length, usage}.

/v1/compact/rerank: accepts candidate list + query, returns score-ordered list. Contract: stable scoring range [0,1]; tie-breaker uses candidate index deterministic behavior. Latency budget tighter on rerank to support synchronous UXs.

Schema samples and minimal cURL examples are in Confluence (see links). All endpoints return error shapes standardized to {code, message, details[]} and surface a 'compatibilityVersion' header to allow future rolling upgrades.
non_functional_requirements: Latency SLOs (compact tier): chat p50<60ms p95<220ms p99<500ms for payloads <=256 tokens when routed to dedicated compact nodes.
Completions p95<180ms for short prompts (<128 tokens); embeddings p95<120ms for 1k-token inputs; rerank p95<150ms for up to 100 candidates.
Availability: 99.9% for compact endpoints across us-west-2 and eu-west-1 during launch window (measured at the API gateway).
Unit cost target: bundled pricing must be within 15% of modeled cost for baseline workloads (see cost model spreadsheet).
Security: payload encryption in transit; customer data is logged only per 'compact' retention policy (14 days by default) unless enterprise opt-in. KMS integration deferred to phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: API contracts implemented and documented in Confluence + OpenAPI spec published in /api/compact/openapi.yaml.
Automated integration tests: cross-language smoke tests pass for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank in CI with coverage >= 90% for critical paths.
Load test profile: compact bundle sustains 2x expected launch traffic with p95 within SLOs; results uploaded to the launch dashboard.
Telemetry coverage: request/response tracing with token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency histograms, and per-model error rates (all dashboards linked).
Canary rollout plan validated: canary handles 1%->10%->50% traffic with automated guardrails; manual approval required for 50%->100% cutover.
Backward compatibility shim for legacy 'stop_sequence' present and tested; deprecation note included in docs with migration examples.
Security checklist signed: threat model review complete, basic abuse detection heuristics in place (rate limiting, anomaly detection), and legal sign-off obtained for the compact retention policy.
Support & runbook: runbooks created for common failure modes (latency spike, model OOM, routing fallback) with escalation paths and Slack paging integration.
scope_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision A: Phase 1 will prioritize predictable latency and a minimal contract. Advanced features (tool-calling, multimodal attachments, long-context streaming beyond 8k tokens) are deferred to phase 2. Tradeoff: narrower use cases at launch in exchange for lower implementation risk and faster time-to-market.

Decision B: Rerank returns normalized scores 0-1; we will not expose internal scoring logits. Tradeoff: less raw signal for some customers but simpler upgrade surface and privacy/responsibility benefits.
Negotiation lever 1 (if timeline slips): drop the deterministic encoding flag from embeddings and ship a stable default mapping; flag to ship in a follow-up patch.
Negotiation lever 2 (if infra capacity constrained): launch GA in single region (us-west-2) and restrict EU customers to beta; migrate EU in release+1.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfooding for 2 weeks (customer success + growth apps).
Phase 1 Canary: route 1% traffic for 24h -> automated checks -> 10% for 3 days -> 50% for 48h (manual go/no-go) -> 100% if metrics green.

Fallback policy: automatic fallback to compatible 'compact-compat' variant with older kernel when certain error thresholds exceeded; outage SLA uses redirection to 'best-effort' lane rather than failure.
Communication: pre-launch blog + changelog, API deprecation emails to users with legacy behavior, and a migration guide in docs.
Cutover checklist: DB migrations (non-blocking), gateway feature flags toggled, OpenAPI published, SDK bumps released, billing toggles enabled.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: compact/api-latency, compact/error-rates, compact/cost-per-token; alert if p95 > SLO for 10m or error rate > 0.5% for 5m.
SLO burn policy: automated paging to SRE when user-facing SLO burn projected to exceed 5% in the next hour.
On-call runbook links included in runbook artifacts. Post-incident report template prepared and assigned to owner for first 30 days.
Usage telemetry must capture model, tokens_in, tokens_out, route, compatibilityVersion, and latency buckets for downstream cost reconciliation.
test_plan: Unit tests for API validation and error shapes.
Integration tests: end-to-end smoke tests against a staging model replica for all endpoints.
Load tests: simulate 2x expected peak with realistic token distributions (mix of chat and embeddings); results committed to the launch dashboard.
Chaos tests: simulate model container eviction and degraded KV cache behavior to verify fallbacks and no data loss.
Security tests: basic fuzzing of request shapes and size limits; rate-limiting validation.
launch_checklist: Docs: PRD -> Confluence published, OpenAPI spec published, migration guide available.
Engineering: API implemented, integration tests green, canary automation in place, rollback path validated, telemetry wired.
SRE/Infra: dedicated compact node pool configured, autoscaling policy defined, capacity reserved for launch week.
DX/SDKs: minimal SDK stubs updated with example configs and release notes.
Legal/Security: retention & privacy policy accepted, security review completed, billing plan validated.
Support: runbooks written, support playbook rehearsed with CS, first-response SLA documented.
Go/No-Go: Product + Eng + SRE + Security sign-off at 50% canary checkpoint.
